Rule: Project creation requires an owning tenant, company, project manager, base currency, timezone, and lifecycle template.
A project may not enter Construction until required preconstruction gates are approved or formally waived.
Approved estimate values become the initial control budget through a traceable import, not direct copy-over.
Original budget, contract value, and approved baselines are immutable; adjustments use controlled revisions.
Only one active approved schedule baseline may exist per baseline type and project.
Progress updates must use a defined data date and retain prior schedule-update snapshots.
Daily reports may be edited until submitted; post-approval corrections require a revision record.
Labor, equipment, and production entries must map to authorized cost codes and project locations when required.
Document revisions never overwrite prior revisions and must clearly identify the current revision.
RFI and submittal responses cannot be treated as contract changes unless routed through change management.
Change events must separately identify scope, cost, schedule, risk, and contractual impacts.
Committed cost must originate from an approved commitment or approved controlled exception.
Forecast-at-completion must reconcile approved budget, commitments, actual costs, pending changes, and remaining forecast.
External users may access only explicitly shared records and redacted fields within an active access period.
Offline changes require conflict checks against server versions before writeback.
AI recommendations remain advisory until accepted by an authorized user; high-impact actions require approval.
Digital twin snapshots must preserve source timestamps and data freshness indicators.
Safety incidents and serious quality events require immediate escalation under tenant-defined thresholds.
Project closeout requires completion or approved waiver of defined closeout deliverables.
All material actions and approvals must create immutable audit events.
